notes: kb/Work PB5074 holds the mechanism in part (BindSetTo and BindSetUpDown bind the later editions' arithmetic-expression); it lists §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR2, SR3 and SR4, not this format row, an expression with an operator or an index-name amount. §1985:VI.6.23.2 prints four formats: Format 1 sends index-name-2, identifier-2 or integer-1 to one or more index-names or identifiers; Format 2 moves one or more index-names UP BY or DOWN BY identifier-3 or integer-2; Format 3 sets groups of mnemonic-names TO ON or OFF, the group repeatable; Format 4 sets one or more condition-names TO TRUE, once. The four are implemented and the later formats are refused at 85: Select chooses a format from the categories of the receivers, and a receiver of a later category cannot be declared at 85 (USAGE POINTER is COBOL0900), so only the Format 1 and Format 2 rows are reached and ReportNoFormat names only those (a non-index receiver of UP BY is COBOL2112 citing §1985:VI.6.23.2); VisitSetBooleanStatement refuses TO FALSE and a second condition-name group (COBOL0900), VisitSetToStatement the ADDRESS OF forms, and LAST EXCEPTION is refused by its own gate. What is NOT implemented is the 1985 sending operand: setToSender and setIndexStatement parse an arithmeticExpression, and BindSetTo (through IndexAssignmentSenderOf, which reads any non-reference as arithmetic-expression-1) and BindSetUpDown bind it with no edition arm, so SET IX TO N + 1, SET IX TO (3), SET IX UP BY N * 2 and SET IX UP BY IY (an index-name amount) compile and run at 85; the arithmetic expression is the 2023 operand the row's change record names. The witness runs the four formats with index-name, identifier and integer senders only.

next.reason: §1985:VI.6.23.2 sends index-name-2, identifier-2 or integer-1 in Format 1 and identifier-3 or integer-2 in Format 2, and §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR2 to SR4 require integers ('Identifier-3 must reference an elementary numeric integer', 'Integer-1 must be positive'); Format 4 is condition-name TO TRUE only. §2023:14.9.39.2 takes arithmetic-expression-1 and arithmetic-expression-2 as those operands, adds TO FALSE and repeated condition-name groups, and adds further formats (object reference, attribute and others). A 1985 SET means the same, but a non-integer sending value, refused at compile time in 1985, is accepted in 2023 and becomes a run-time exception condition: §2023:14.9.39.4 GR2 ('If the value of arithmetic-expression-1 does not result in an integer ... the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT exception condition is set to exist') and §2023:14.9.39.4 GR3 for arithmetic-expression-2. Wider syntax plus a refusal made an exception condition: CHANGED.
